teaser.text: Edwards Lifesciences is a medical-device company whose products help heart teams repair or replace failing valves. Its business is easiest to understand as a chain: a hospital chooses a device for an approved procedure, Edwards supplies and supports it, and the proceeds pay for making the next one.

blocks.heading: Where could Edwards Lifesciences’ shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted price is $73.78 in October 2027, a 15% loss including dividends. It is $76.25 in October 2028, a 12% loss. By October 2029, the weighted price reaches $77.56, still a 10% loss. Bear probability is 28%, while base probability is 55%. Bull probability is 17%.
At October 2029, the range runs from $48.69 to $117.42. Today’s price is $86.60. Because every scenario assumes no dividend, the returns come entirely from the share price.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Edwards Lifesciences?

paragraphs.text: The base follows the steady rise in adjusted earnings across the historical record, while 2026 guidance calls for strong sales growth and operating-margin expansion. The next-twelve-month EPS estimate also supports earnings near $2 billion. The model excludes the latest quarter’s deferred-tax allowance and impairment, plus the earlier disposal gain, because they are not recurring operating profit. The bear case assumes slower TAVR, limited TMTT scaling and cost pressure. The bull case requires stronger patient growth, broader TMTT adoption and more operating leverage.

The bear path combines weaker operations with valuation compression. TAVR growth slows, hospital capacity limits procedures, and TMTT remains concentrated in early centers. Legal, tax and launch costs restrict margin recovery. The path begins at $55.33 and ends at $48.69. Its probability is 28% because these risks are visible, although historical adjusted earnings growth makes sustained contraction less likely than the base case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Edwards Lifesciences really make?

paragraphs.text: Profit and cash differ because accounting records income when it is earned, while cash flow records when money arrives and leaves. Customers may pay after Edwards records a sale, and expenses such as depreciation or stock compensation may reduce profit without an immediate cash payment. Operating cash flow reached $1,595.2 million in 2025, helped by better operations and lower tax payments after the unusually heavy cash-tax burden associated with the 2024 Critical Care sale.

blocks.heading: What has Edwards Lifesciences guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: After a stronger second quarter, management raised its full-year constant-currency sales-growth outlook to 10.0%–11.0% and its TAVR growth outlook to 8.0%–9.0%. It also lifted its TMTT sales outlook to $760–$780 million. Constant currency estimates growth as if exchange rates had not changed, so it gives a clearer view of underlying demand.

But Edwards kept its adjusted EPS outlook at $2.95–$3.05. EPS is profit per share after costs and taxes, so sales can rise without earnings rising equally. The company said its effective tax rate would be at the high end of its earlier range. Its adjusted figure also excludes selected items such as some litigation costs, intangible-asset amortization and impairment losses; GAAP profit remains the accounting result investors must examine.

Edwards expects R&D to remain about 17% of sales in 2026 and forecasts 150 basis points of constant-currency operating-margin expansion. The investment goes toward clinical evidence, new structural-heart products and existing therapies. That spending is the price of the growth promise, which makes analysts’ lower earnings expectations the next question.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Edwards Lifesciences' next results?

paragraphs.text: Edwards still expected several fourth-quarter milestones: U.S. FDA approval of PASCAL for tricuspid regurgitation, a next-generation PASCAL system with Capture Clarity, a U.S. tricuspid PASCAL launch and PROGRESS results at TCT. The company also scheduled an investor Q&A at TCT for November 2, 2026, and its third-quarter earnings call for November 4, 2026. Those events will show whether the pipeline is becoming a business, not merely an approved idea.
